Hi Laura / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at Ovation is excited to move into a two-week pilot starting next month. Before we lock dates with IT, procurement asked us to confirm a couple of items that are blocking their approval:

- We need an explicit SLO for the pilot window (uptime + p95 latency target) and a clear statement of how rate limits/quotas will be handled if we spike during onboarding.
- During the first 48–72 hours of onboarding we anticipate elevated traffic (spikes up to ~3x our steady-state QPS) while we warm caches and run batch migrations. We’d like a temporary override (or a "tie-breaker") to your fairness/throttling policy so that our onboarding traffic isn't deprioritized relative to other customers.

I've attached a short traffic summary and the pilot plan (traffic-patterns.csv, pilot-plan.pdf) with expected QPS and time windows. Procurement has asked for a one-page note on the operational guardrails for such an override: what telemetry you'll monitor, any automatic fallbacks, and whether this impacts SLA credits or billing.

Can you confirm if Redwood can provide a short-term carveout and the terms (duration, monitoring, cost)? Procurement would like that language included in a simple addendum to the pilot MSA.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — looking to finalize by next Friday.

Best,
Avery Clark

Marissa / team — reviewed Ovation's traffic file and pilot plan. Summary and proposed constraints below.

Quoted from Avery's traffic summary:
> peak bursts up to ~3x steady-state QPS, bursts are concentrated during initial onboarding and batch migrations.

SRE recommendation (operational carveout):
- Temporary burst allowance: allow up to 2.5x steady-state QPS for a maximum window of 72 hours from the official pilot kickoff.
- Throttle policy: bursts are allowed only if CPU/GPU utilization on the hosting pool remains < 70%. If utilization crosses 70% for 5 continuous minutes, automatic throttling will reduce Ovation's burst back to steady-state levels.
- Telemetry/monitoring: we will enable a dedicated dashboard that includes per-route QPS, token throughput, p95 latency, GPU utilization, and a fairness_metric. Alerts will be configured for (a) p95 > 500ms for 3m, (b) fairness_metric > 0.8, (c) GPU utilization > 75%.
- Billing and SLA: bursts under the carveout will be billable at an overage rate (2.5x multiplier on per-token price for the burst window). SLA uptime (99.9%) and latency SLOs remain measured across normal traffic; during automatic throttling events caused by platform capacity safety, we will not apply SLA credits for the portions where system-level throttling was active.
- Safety & rollback: an automatic fallback route will redirect overflow traffic to a compatible, lower-throughput model variant (cheaper model) if we detect sustained capacity pressure.

Attached is a short params file with specific thresholds (carveout-params.yaml). We should also require Ovation to provide a signed operational addendum acknowledging the billing and rollback behavior before the carveout is enabled.

If Sales/legal agree, we can surface a one-page addendum and schedule the dashboard prep.

—Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: carveout-params.yaml

Hi Avery / Ovation procurement team —

Thanks for the patience while we evaluated this. Per the SRE review and Sales agreement, Redwood can offer a controlled, temporary carveout to the fairness policy for the pilot under the following terms (summary addendum text below). If that works, we'll push an addendum into HubSpot/DocuSign by EOD Monday.

Summary (pilot carveout terms)
- Duration: single 72-hour window starting at the pilot kickoff timestamp you confirm.
- Burst cap: up to 2.5x your steady-state QPS (as provided in your traffic file).
- Safety thresholds: automatic throttling to steady-state if host pool GPU utilization exceeds 70% for 5 continuous minutes.
- Monitoring: Redwood will provide a dedicated dashboard (per-route QPS, p95 latency, GPU util, fairness_metric) and alerting.
- Billing: burst usage in the carveout window billed at an overage multiplier (2.5x per-token price).
- SLA credit: SLA uptime/latency SLOs remain in force; however, outages or throttling events triggered by platform-level safety actions during the carveout window are excluded from SLA credits.
- Required approvals: Ovation procurement must sign an operational addendum acknowledging the billing and rollback behavior; carving-in requires legal counter-signature prior to enabling.

Next steps
1) Marissa will add the one-page addendum to the HubSpot deal and route to your procurement for signature (HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/OV-2026-1125-PLT).
2) Rishi will provision the monitoring dashboard and carveout flags once the signed addendum is received.
3) We will schedule the kickoff & canary run — suggested date range Dec 8–10, please confirm availability.

If that aligns with your procurement requirements we’ll generate the addendum. If you need alternative billing or a different duration, let us know and we’ll loop legal.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Laura Bennett
